correctness.rationale: For an infinite-dimensional abstract AL lattice E and any bounded T:E→Y, pairwise disjoint unit vectors have ||Σa_nx_n||=Σ|a_n|; every disjointly generated span is isometric to ℓ1, whence ||T|M(x)||=sup_n||Tx_n||. Passing to a subsequence approaching liminf gives Γ_d(T)=β(T). For arbitrary lattice-domain R, if on every tail of a given disjoint sequence there were norm-one vectors whose image lay uniformly below β(R), finitely supported approximants in successive disjoint blocks would contradict the defining infimum β(R). This yields β≤κ_d; κ_d≤Γ_d follows from injection modulus≤operator norm. Thus the three coincide in AL spaces. Disjoint-coordinate spans inherit precisely the same ambient disjointness, proving Δ_d(T)=sup_x β(T|M(x)). González–Martinón (2021) Proposition 4.5 supplies Γ_d(T+S)≤Γ_d(T)+Δ_d(S); symmetrization yields the sharp β perturbation bound, identity operator shows coefficient 1. Proposition 4.4 supplies DSS⇔Δ_d=0. No numerical samples can replace this infinite-dimensional argument.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The general-domain 2021 comparisons and perturbation inequalities are broader in domain but weaker in constants; Example 6.3 demonstrates they cannot imply an unrestricted Γ_d=β equality. AL additivity is the extra class hypothesis used for the sharp identity; the broad general theorem is therefore not a dominating result.
